headline: Every unit checked, not a sample.
label: #FFFFFF
heroLede: Doubling output at Braeside means twice the labels and codes to get right. Here's what a camera check could look like on your filling lines. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every unit has its cap or pump on, straight and fully closed. A loose cap means a leak in the carton and a complaint from the pharmacy.
labelLede: A moisturising cream and a gentle wash can share a pack and look much the same at line speed. The camera checks every unit carries the right label for the product, straight and intact.
codeLede: The batch and expiry code ties every unit back to its batch. The system reads the printed code on every unit and compares it with the product and batch set at changeover.
objectLede: Cap offcuts, glove pieces and loose parts can end up on the conveyor. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a carton.

vocab.alert: Four crooked caps in fifteen minutes. Check the capper.
